title: Projective cosimplicial resolutions paired with injective simplicial weights
statement:
Use the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence and Reedy conventions of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and simplicial sets with the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Fix a small ordinary category $J$ and containing universes. Let $\mathcal M$ be any model category for which $\mathcal M^J$ has the projective model structure, with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. Let $V^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M^J$ be Reedy cofibrant in this projective model category, and suppose every cosimplicial structure map is an objectwise weak equivalence. Give $\mathrm{sSet}^{J^{\mathrm{op}}}$ the injective model structure of [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model], whose weak equivalences and cofibrations are objectwise. For $K:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and $T\in\mathcal M$, define
$$L_VK=\int^{j\in J}\int^{[n]\in\Delta}V^n(j)\cdot K(j)_n,\qquad (R_VT)(j)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(V^n(j),T).$$
Here $Z\cdot S=\coprod_{s\in S}Z$, the coend is the coproduct modulo the relations induced by arrows of $J$ and $\Delta$, and the simplicial operators and the $J^{\mathrm{op}}$-action of $R_VT$ are precomposition. These formulas define an adjunction $L_V\dashv R_V$. The functor $L_V$ sends objectwise monomorphisms to cofibrations in $\mathcal M$, and sends objectwise monomorphisms that are objectwise weak homotopy equivalences to trivial cofibrations. Thus this is a Quillen adjunction for the injective structure on its source. No simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal M$, no properness hypothesis, and no nonemptiness condition on $J$ are imposed.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Model Categories and Their Localizations, Lemma 19.2.14(1), Theorem 19.3.1(1) and Theorem 19.4.4, printed pp.411–415 (PDF pp.425–429). Agent adaptation of the weighted-coend lifting calculation: projective cofibrancy is imposed on the entire cosimplicial diagram and weights carry the injective model structure. This strengthened interchange is not asserted to be the literal statement of 19.3.1, whose weights are projective. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Write $E(A,K)$ for the double coend of the statement, for any cosimplicial $J$-diagram $A$. A map $E(A,K)\to T$ is exactly a family of maps $A_j^n\to T$ indexed by $x\in K(j)_n$, satisfying the $J$ and simplex relations. Equivalently it is a natural simplicial map $K\to R_AT$. The assignments in both directions are inverse on each coprojection and commute with maps of $K,T$. This proves the asserted adjunction, including its precomposition operators. All coends exist because $J$ and $\Delta$ are small and $\mathcal M$ is cocomplete. The same coprojection description shows that $E$ preserves colimits separately in its two arguments.

source.place: Lemma 19.2.14 and its preceding adjointness calculation; explicit copower adjunction

proof.text:
First consider $u:X\to Y$ in the projective model on $\mathcal M^J$ and an objectwise injection $v:S\to T$ of set presheaves. For a map $p:Z\to Z'$ in $\mathcal M$, lifting $u\square_Jv$ against $p$ is equivalent, by [lem-coef-parametrized-adjunction-corner-lifting] applied to the parametrized adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X\odot_JS,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M^J}(X,Z^{S(-)})$ given by the coprojection calculation of Step 1, to lifting $u$ against the $J$-diagram map with component
$$Z^{T(j)}\longrightarrow Z^{S(j)}\times_{(Z')^{S(j)}}(Z')^{T(j)},$$
where powers mean products, and presheaf restriction induces its covariant $J$ action. At $j$ choose a complement to $S(j)\subseteq T(j)$; this map is isomorphic to an identity on $Z^{S(j)}$ times the product of copies of $p$ over that complement. Products and pullbacks of maps in a right lifting class remain in that class: each lifting problem is solved componentwise. Thus the displayed map is an objectwise trivial fibration if $p$ is trivial, and an objectwise fibration if $p$ is a fibration. By the projective lifting axioms, $u\square_Jv$ is a cofibration when $u$ is a cofibration, and is a trivial cofibration when $u$ is trivial. Complements need not be natural; only the classification of each component uses them.

source.place: Agent lifting calculation for projective diagrams paired with injective set weights

proof.text: If $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ is objectwise monic, its relative simplicial latching maps $\delta_ni$ are objectwise injections: by [lem-coef-simplicial-latching-degenerate-subset], naturally in $j$ the latching presheaf maps injectively onto the subset of degenerate $n$-simplices, and a simplex $x$ of $K(j)$ that is degenerate in $L(j)$ is already degenerate in $K(j)$: write $x=L(j)(\sigma)y$ with $\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$, $r<n$, choose a section $\delta$ of $\sigma$, and then $y=L(j)(\delta)x\in K(j)_r$. Hence $K(j)_n\cap D_nL(j)=D_nK(j)$. Apply [lem-coef-weighted-coend-skeletal-filtration] to a Reedy projective cofibration $f:A\to A'$. Step 2 shows each transition in its filtration is a cofibration. They are trivial cofibrations if $f$ is Reedy trivial, since its relative latching maps are then projective trivial cofibrations by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Pushouts and countable composites of left lifting classes remain in the class, by successively constructing lifts and using the colimit at the last stage. Thus the corner $E(f,i)$ is a cofibration, trivial whenever $f$ is Reedy trivial. Taking $f:0\to V$ proves that $L_V$ preserves every objectwise monomorphism.

Fix any $K$. Taking $i:\varnothing\to K$ in Step 3 shows that $F_K:A\mapsto E(A,K)$ sends Reedy projective trivial cofibrations to trivial cofibrations. It therefore preserves weak equivalences between Reedy projective cofibrant objects. Indeed, for such a weak equivalence $f:A\to A'$, apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] in the Reedy projective model category to obtain $f=pi$, $ps=1$ with $i,s$ cofibrations and $p$ a trivial fibration. Two-out-of-three makes both $i,s$ trivial. Then $F_Ki,F_Ks$ are weak equivalences; $F_Kp F_Ks=1$ makes $F_Kp$ weak by two-out-of-three, and hence $F_Kf$ is weak. No fibrancy assumption is used.

Each $V_j$ is a cosimplicial resolution. To check the cofibrancy assertion, evaluation at $j$ is left Quillen on the projective model: its right adjoint sends $Z$ at $k$ to $\prod_{\operatorname{Hom}_J(k,j)}Z$, so preserves objectwise fibrations and trivial fibrations by componentwise lifting. Evaluation commutes with latching colimits, and therefore sends the projective cofibrations $L_nV\to V^n$ to cofibrations. Homotopical constancy is a hypothesis. The colimit-preserving functor $T_j(K)=V_j^\bullet\otimes_\Delta K$ sends $\partial\Delta^n\to\Delta^n$ to this evaluated latching map and sends simplex collapses to the structure maps $V_j^n\to V_j^0$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], $T_j$ sends horns to trivial cofibrations and all weak equivalences to weak equivalences.

The same coend $G(K)=E(V,K)$, considered on the projective model of simplicial presheaves, is left Quillen. For $h_j(k)=\operatorname{Hom}_J(k,j)$, the $J$-relations give $G(h_j\times S)\cong V_j^\bullet\otimes_\Delta S$, by applying $V(a)$ on the summand indexed by $a:k\to j$, with inverse the identity-arrow summand. The boundary and horn generators in [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] are therefore sent to cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by Step 5. Equivalently the right adjoint $R_V$ sends (trivial) fibrations to objectwise (trivial) Kan fibrations, by testing boundaries and horns through this displayed identification. The projective weak factorization systems then give the Quillen assertion. Applying exactly the Brown split argument of Step 4 in this projective presheaf model shows that $G$ preserves weak equivalences between projectively cofibrant presheaves.

Apply [lem-coef-framed-projective-diagram-resolution] to $V$, obtaining $PV\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}V$, Reedy projective cofibrant at the source and target and a weak equivalence in that model. Step 4 yields natural weak equivalences $E(PV,K)\to E(V,K)$ for every $K$, without any cofibrancy requirement on the weight.

Put $I=J^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply [lem-coef-free-bar-cell-filtration] to the $I$-diagram $K$ to obtain the functorial projectively cofibrant presheaf
$$QK(j)=\int^{[p]}\coprod_{j\to j_0\to\cdots\to j_p}K(j_p)\times\Delta^p.$$
Its faces are numbered in $I$: $d_0$ applies the contravariant $K$ action at $j_p$, $d_p$ composes the arrows at the $j$ end, and internal faces compose the intervening arrows. At each $j$ its augmented simplicial bar object has the terminal extra-degeneracy maps and identities stated in that node. This bar object is Reedy cofibrant in $\mathrm{sSet}$: latching objects in $\mathrm{sSet}$ are computed in each inner degree $r$, where [lem-coef-simplicial-latching-degenerate-subset] applied to the simplicial set $[p]\mapsto P_p(j)_r$ identifies the latching set with the degenerate subset, the subcoproduct indexed by chains containing an identity internal arrow. The inclusion is a monomorphism, hence a cofibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The presheaf-model node says the Kan model is simplicial. Thus [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-extra-degeneracy] applies and makes $QK(j)\to K(j)$ weak. For an objectwise weak equivalence $a:K\to L$, naturality of these augmentations and two-out-of-three make $Qa$ objectwise weak. Both its endpoints are projectively cofibrant, so Step 6 makes $E(V,Qa)$ weak.

There is a natural isomorphism $E(PV,K)\cong E(V,QK)$. Expand the formula defining $PV$ in [lem-coef-framed-projective-diagram-resolution] and interchange its coproducts and coequalizers. The $J$-coend replaces the last arrow $j_p\to j$ and its $K(j)$-label by $K(j_p)$. The remaining $\Delta$-coend uses
$$\int^{[n]}(\Delta^n)_r\times K(j_p)_n\cong K(j_p)_r,$$
whose map sends $(\alpha:[r]\to[n],x)$ to $K(\alpha)x$, with inverse $x\mapsto(1_{[r]},x)$. Both sides consequently have the same coprojections
$$\coprod_{j_0\to\cdots\to j_p}V_{j_0}^r\cdot(K(j_p)_r\times(\Delta^p)_r)$$
and the same arrow, simplex and bar-face relations: $d_0$ applies the contravariant $K$ action at $j_p$, $d_p$ applies $V$ at $j_0$, and the interior faces compose arrows. The final-vertex numbering in the definition of $P$ is essential here. This also proves naturality in $K$. Thus Step 8 makes $E(PV,a)$ a weak equivalence. In the natural commutative square with horizontal maps $E(PV,a)$ and $E(V,a)$, both vertical maps are weak equivalences by Step 7. Two-out-of-three proves that $E(V,a)$ is weak for every objectwise weak equivalence $a$.

If $a$ is also objectwise monic, Step 3 makes $E(V,a)$ a cofibration and Step 9 makes it weak, hence it is a trivial cofibration. The injective model structure exists by [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model], since the Kan model is combinatorial by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Its cofibrations and trivial cofibrations are exactly the two classes just treated. Together with Step 1 this proves the stated Quillen adjunction. For $J=\varnothing$ the source diagram category has one object, $L_V$ is the initial object of $\mathcal M$, $R_V$ the unique diagram, and the only image map is an identity, so all clauses hold. The argument nowhere assumes simplicial enrichment or properness of $\mathcal M$.
